scenes.title: Is the abundance excess larger than its uncertainty?

scenes.title: Different methods can fake different physics
scenes.narration: This review asks why two surveys can report different galaxy metallicities before the galaxies themselves differ. It separates three effects that are often mixed together: calibration scale, aperture, and diffuse ionized gas.
scenes.callout: A comparison checklist · not a new measurement

scenes.title: Absolute scales differ by up to 0.7 dex
scenes.narration: Theoretical photoionization calibrations and empirical electron-temperature calibrations can differ by roughly 0.7 dex in absolute oxygen abundance. That is about a factor of five before any physical evolution is inferred.
scenes.callout: Literature threshold · not measured by this draft

scenes.title: A small fiber is not a whole galaxy
scenes.narration: Below about twenty percent covering fraction, a fixed fiber can bias metallicity by more than 0.15 dex. Central regions are typically richer, so the aperture can manufacture mass trends and even a false turnover.
scenes.callout: Correct or floor the covering fraction

scenes.title: Integrated spectra mix two environments
scenes.narration: Diffuse ionized gas can supply thirty to sixty percent of H-alpha emission. Its harder spectrum boosts low-ionization line ratios, which can flatten or even invert the metallicity gradients inferred from integrated light.
scenes.callout: Resolved maps provide an independent check

scenes.title: Three rules for a fair comparison
scenes.narration: Use one declared abundance scale with published conversions. Enforce covering-fraction floors or calibrated aperture corrections. Then use integral-field spectroscopy as the independent ground truth for the integrated relation.
scenes.callout: Separate systematics before interpreting evolution

scenes.title: A methods synthesis · not peer review
scenes.narration: The contribution is this framework, not a new metallicity measurement. The thresholds come from published literature. Automated review-cleared status is a workflow gate, not human or journal peer review. The draft is not validated.
scenes.callout: Literature-sourced thresholds · explicit provenance

scenes.title: Matching z≈0 does not validate evolution
scenes.narration: IllustrisTNG is calibrated to selected local observations. This paper tests it away from that tuning point. The key move is to subtract TNG's own local residual before comparing its evolution with SDSS and JWST.

scenes.title: TNG already misses both local relations
scenes.narration: At redshift zero, TNG's star-forming main sequence sits 0.30 dex below SDSS, while its mass-metallicity relation sits 0.12 dex above. Those offsets are systematic starting errors, not high-redshift evolution.

scenes.title: The robust discrepancy is over-growth
scenes.narration: After removing the starting error, TNG's internal main-sequence growth is plus 1.30, 1.45, and 1.61 dex at redshifts four, five, and six. Observations rise only about 0.9 to 1.0 dex.
